root_cause.text: tmigr_handle_remote_cpu() in the timer migration subsystem incorrectly skipped timer_expire_remote() for the local CPU based on the stale assumption that the local softirq had already expired all local global-wheel timers, ignoring that jiffies can advance between run_timer_base(BASE_GLOBAL) and remote expiry evaluation.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says “This assumption is wrong because jiffies can advance after the handling of the CPU's global timers in run_timer_base(BASE_GLOBAL) and before tmigr_handle_remote() evaluates the expiry times,” and the patch removes the `if (cpu != smp_processor_id())` guard so `timer_expire_remote(cpu)` is called unconditionally.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always invoke `timer_expire_remote()` for the target CPU, including the local CPU, to avoid missing timer expiration when `jiffies` advances during timer migration handling.
intent_record.what: The conditional call `if (cpu != smp_processor_id()) timer_expire_remote(cpu);` was replaced with an unconditional call to `timer_expire_remote(cpu);`, and a comment was added explaining that the local CPU must not be excluded because `jiffies` may advance between `run_timer_base(BASE_GLOBAL)` and the earlier `jiffies` snapshot taken in `tmigr_handle_remote()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `timer_expire_remote(cpu)` is now invoked even when `cpu` is the current CPU, ensuring timer expiration handling is not skipped for the local CPU in a timing window where `jiffies` has advanced. This prevents missed or delayed timer processing caused by the previous local-CPU exclusion.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by removing the incorrect special-casing of the local CPU and always calling `timer_expire_remote()` for it as well, preventing missed timer expiration when `jiffies` advances during timer migration handling.

candidates.rationale: This conditional embodies the faulty assumption that the local CPU does not need remote expiry handling. By excluding the local CPU, it can skip timer_expire_remote() when jiffies advanced after local global-wheel expiration, leading to missed timer expiration.

This call is only reached under the buggy condition excluding the local CPU. It is the operation that should have been invoked for all target CPUs, including the local one, to avoid missing expired timers.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional is the root faulty check: it skips remote timer expiry handling when the target CPU is the local CPU, based on the stale assumption that local global-wheel timers were already fully expired. If jiffies advances after run_timer_base(BASE_GLOBAL) and before this evaluation, expired timers can be missed because timer_expire_remote() is not invoked for the local CPU.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains the full body of the relevant function `tmigr_handle_remote_cpu()`, including the decision whether to call `timer_expire_remote(cpu)`. The vulnerable construct is present in this commit. In `tmigr_handle_remote_cpu()`, after dropping `tmc->lock`, the code does: `if (cpu != smp_processor_id()) timer_expire_remote(cpu);` This explicitly skips `timer_expire_remote()` when the target CPU is the local CPU. That matches the root cause: local-CPU remote-expiry handling is skipped based on the assumption that local global-wheel timers were already expired by the local softirq. The root cause says this assumption is stale because `jiffies` can advance between `run_timer_base(BASE_GLOBAL)` and remote expiry evaluation, so the local CPU may still need `timer_expire_remote()`. There is no compensating logic here to handle the local CPU in that case; instead the function simply omits the call for `cpu == smp_processor_id()`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet included.
